facts.statement: The holotype specimen UMNH VP 20208 was discovered in 2004 by Andrew R. C. Milner.
facts.quote: The holotype of Hippodraco, UMNH VP 20208, was discovered in 2004 by Andrew R. C. Milner.

facts.statement: The genus was named in 2010 by Andrew T. McDonald, James I. Kirkland, Andrew R. C. Milner, Scott K. Madsen, Donald D. DeBlieux, Jennifer Cavin, and Lukas Panzarin.
facts.quote: It was later named in 2010 by Andrew T. McDonald, James I. Kirkland, Andrew R. C. Milner, Scott K. Madsen, Donald D. DeBlieux, Jennifer Cavin and Lukas Panzarin.

facts.statement: The generic name Hippodraco combines the Greek word for 'horse' and the Latin word for 'dragon'.
facts.quote: The generic name Hippodraco is a combination of the Greek word hippos ("horse") and the Latin word draco ("dragon").

facts.statement: The specific name scutodens references the shield-shaped crowns of the dentary teeth.
facts.quote: The specific name scutodens is a combination of the Latin words scutum (meaning shield) and dens (meaning tooth), and it references the shield-shaped dentary tooth crowns.

facts.statement: The holotype was found at Andrew's Site in the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation, dating to the Valanginian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: UMNH VP 20208 was unearthed from the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation, Utah, at a site known as Andrew's Site, dating from the Valanginian stage in the Early Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: Holtz estimated the weight of the holotype between 227 and 454 kg.
facts.quote: Holtz estimated its weight between 227 to 454 kg.

facts.statement: The preserved left dentary features teeth with shield-shaped crowns.
facts.quote: The left dentary is preserved on the skull along with teeth, which, have shield-shaped crowns.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses from 2010 and 2011 recovered Hippodraco as a basal member of Styracosterna with Theiophytalia as its closest relative.
facts.quote: In 2010 and 2011 cladistic analyses of McDonald and colleagues, Hippodraco has been recovered as a basal member of the Styracosterna and its closest relative was Theiophytalia.

facts.statement: The parent group of Hippodraco is Styracosterna.
Hippodraco belongs to the class Ornithischia.
Hippodraco lived during the Valanginian stage, between 137.05 and 132.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Valanginian (137.05 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Contemporaneous fauna included the ornithopod Cedrorestes, sauropods Cedarosaurus and Moabosaurus, theropods Martharaptor and Nedcolbertia, the nodosaurid Gastonia, and the giant dromaeosaurid Utahraptor.
facts.quote: Contemporaneous fauna from the Upper Yellow Cat include the fellow ornithopod Cedrorestes, sauropods (Cedarosaurus and Moabosaurus), theropods (Martharaptor and Nedcolbertia), the nodosaurid Gastonia, and the giant dromaeosaurid Utahraptor.
